title: Playing with Oliver at the Lincoln Gardens and the plantation
summary: One long answer: first night at Lincoln Gardens, $85 a week, dinner at Stella Oliver's, the Gardens fire, and plans for the Plantation.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, they was working down there and there. Where was Joe playing then? Joe was playing in Lincoln Garden. Lincoln Garden. Louis was working at the Dreamland, and joined the band at the Dreamland. I mean Lil was working there together. So I come to Chicago and I joined Joe's band. Well Joe had George Fields and he had a big band. He had the kind of band that he had now. He had a corner player playing with a man by the name of Bob Schaffner. He went later to the plantation with Dave Payton. So with the band playing, they was playing all the good old tunes from New Orleans. So Joe come down and talked to me on a, Lincoln Garden was packed in jam, King Jones was announced at that time, and he was jumping. Preston Jackson and then a little drum roll player, what's his name again? Al Wynn. Since I've been sick I can't think of nobody's name. Al Wynn, they put me over there in Lincoln Garden. So Joe say, Joe always was a nasty talker you know, Joe put me in the dozens and say, I heard you was there, I heard you could blow. He said, Tio told me you're a human being. I laughed and I laughed and I said, well Joe you know, I can't play like you but I play. He said, what numbers do you know all those numbers you know you've been playing up there? I said, well I know all the standards like Panama and the high society. I know all the good old New Orleans tunes and all the standards. He said, when you be here tomorrow at two o'clock they will have rehearsal. So I stayed to the last note that Joe was playing. I still couldn't sleep. I went home living on Cottage Grove in 3030 at that time, 3310 Cottage Grove. I went home I couldn't sleep because the thrills were thinking that he could sit by the King, King Oliver that time. See, so I went and Joe called Roycele and after we run down about three tunes Joe stopped Roycele and said, well that's enough. He said, you got a tuxedo suit Lee? I said, no man. He said, I ain't got no tuxedo. He said, well I'll just wear your dark suit. He said, be to work tonight. He said, you start to work tonight, 85 a week. 85, I never had any great great 85 a week. I made it, but I never had that kind of salary. Jesus have mercy. 85 a week. I said, so I go to work with Joe and Joe was tickled to death and everything. I said, I'm alright Papa? He said, you're alright. So he said, what you want tomorrow? You come and get them red beans and rice. I have Stella to cook your nice dinner Lee. He said, come on over. He said, I went over there and so Miss Stella met right at the door with smiles and he said, Lee? He said, you Lee here? He said, I said, yes. He said, Joe, Joe, I'm so glad. He said, you made Joe feel good. Joe's sleeping now, but he's going to wake up. He said, Joe, you made Joe feel good by it. He said, Joe says he's happy now. He got a boy sitting inside him. He's just like Lewis plays and he said, the old New Orleans stuff is happy again. So I was glad to hear that. And so we got up and Joe and Oliver and Joe say, well, you sure surprised me, Lee. I said, I'm glad Joe because I really want to play with you. He said, I said, great thrills of my life to come to you in this big time and especially in Chicago. And Joe said, don't worry. You'll be with me a long time, Papa. So we went seven nights a week over gardens. So I went over there cleaning to the gardens caught a fire. The garden on a Christmas Eve night. The gardens had caught a fire. I'd been in with Joe about seven, eight months at that time. And frankly saved all my money I had made. It's all but with the rent I was paying. I saved a few hundred dollars and I never had that kind of cash saved. So Joe say, Joe called me home and said, well, he said, they haven't got that garden ready yet. He said, but I got a chance to go on another good job. He said, what's the good musicians back home? He said, it's going to be a big band. And that time I told him about Lewis Russell. I told him about the drummer, Bob Rand, Bonnie Big Eye. I told him about them. So they come up and Joe sent for them. So we started hoisting for the, going to the plantation. It was going to be Joe Oliver and myself in the old plantation. So, and another corned player because they had a big show. Bob Schaffner, we'll use three corneds. Bob was going to play the show down for us. So it was a pretty tough winter that winter. Oh, I had never seen so much snow in all my life. I was wanting Jesus. I was falling down, walking through that slope, going to rehearsal. And I was disgusted because it's so cold. My heart is freezing up the bowels. I get there to warm up.
